q: Which is the correct electronic configuration of Cr (24) and Cu (29)?
explanation: In Cr, due to the extra stability of the half-filled 3d5 and in Cu of the fully-filled 3d10, one electron moves from 4s to 3d.
subject: Inorganic

q: When Fe2+ is formed from Fe (26), what will be the electronic configuration of Fe2+?
explanation: Fe is [Ar] 3d6 4s2; when an ion is formed, the 4s electrons are removed first.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which has the highest electron affinity?
explanation: The small size of F increases repulsion, so Cl > F; F has the highest electronegativity, not electron affinity.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which statement about first ionisation energy is correct?
options: The IE of Al is greater than that of Mg
The IE of N is greater than that of O
The IE of O is greater than that of N
The IE of B is greater than that of Be
explanation: N has a half-filled, stable 2p3; in O (2p4) paired-electron repulsion is greater, so removing an electron is easier.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is O2 paramagnetic?
options: In the Lewis structure all the electrons are paired
According to MOT, there are 2 unpaired electrons in the pi* antibonding orbital
explanation: Bond order 2, 2 unpaired electrons in pi*; it is explained only by MOT.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is the H-N-H bond angle in NH3 approximately 107° rather than 109.5°?
options: Lone pair-bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair-bond pair repulsion
The N-H bond is longer than the C-H bond
explanation: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair; the lone pair occupies more space, the angle decreases, and the shape is pyramidal.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the correct order of basicity of H3PO2, H3PO3 and H3PO4?
explanation: Basicity is determined by the number of P-OH groups; P-H groups are not counted.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the shape of XeF4?
explanation: sp3d2, 2 lone pairs, square planar; XeF2 is linear.
subject: Inorganic

q: What type are the bridging hydrogen bonds in diborane (B2H6)?
explanation: 4 normal terminal B-H + 2 bridging B-H-B, one electron pair shared between 3 atoms.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the spin-only magnetic moment of high-spin Fe3+ (d5)?
explanation: mu = sqrt(n(n+2)); n=5 gives sqrt(35) ≈ 5.92 BM.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which of the following is a primary standard?
explanation: K2Cr2O7 is pure, stable and can be weighed easily; KMnO4 is not a primary standard.
subject: Inorganic

q: According to Werner theory, how many Cl- ions per formula unit of [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 will precipitate with AgNO3?
explanation: Only the 2 outer Cl- ions are ionisable (primary valency); the inner one is bound in the coordination sphere.
subject: Inorganic

q: What will be the CFSE of an octahedral low-spin d6 complex (t2g6 eg0)? (Ignoring pairing energy)
explanation: Each t2g electron contributes -0.4Δo; 6 × (-0.4Δo) = -2.4Δo.
subject: Inorganic

q: What are the geometry and magnetic behaviour of [Ni(CN)4]2-?
explanation: CN- is a strong-field ligand, the electrons pair up, dsp2, square planar, 0 unpaired electrons, diamagnetic.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which of the following is a Lewis base?
explanation: A Lewis base is an electron-pair donor; NH3 donates a lone pair; BF3, AlCl3 and H+ are Lewis acids.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which statement about photochemical smog is correct?
options: It is formed in winter from smoke and fog
O3 and PAN are formed in it and it is oxidising
explanation: In sunlight, NOx + hydrocarbons form ozone/PAN; SO2 is a component of classical (London) smog.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which metal ion and oxidation state is present in haemoglobin for oxygen transport?
explanation: In heme there is Fe2+; the oxidation state remains +2 even on binding O2; Mg2+ is in chlorophyll.
subject: Inorganic

q: H2O2 is both an oxidising agent and a reducing agent — what is the reason?
options: The oxidation state of O is 0
The oxidation state of O is -1
The oxidation state of O is -2
explanation: O is -1, between O2 (0) and H2O (-2), so it can go in both directions.
subject: Inorganic

q: The froth flotation process is used for the concentration of which type of ore?
explanation: Sulphide particles stick to oil/froth and rise up, while the gangue remains below.
subject: Inorganic

q: The brown ring test is for the identification of which ion?
explanation: With FeSO4 + conc. H2SO4, a brown ring of the [Fe(H2O)5(NO)]2+ complex is formed.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which is the most resonance-stabilised ion?
explanation: In phenoxide the negative charge is delocalised in the ring; it is not delocalised in an alkoxide.
subject: Organic

q: What is the correct order of C-H bond acidity?
explanation: s-character: sp 50% > sp2 33% > sp3 25%; the alkyne H is the most acidic.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the most stable carbocation?
explanation: +I effect and 9 alpha-H hyperconjugation; 3° > 2° > 1° > CH3+.
subject: Organic

q: Why is meso-tartaric acid optically inactive despite having 2 chiral centres?
options: It has an internal plane of symmetry
It does not dissolve in an achiral solvent
explanation: Internal compensation.
subject: Organic

q: What is the major product of the Br2/hν bromination of propane?
explanation: The 2° free radical is more stable, and bromination is selective.
subject: Organic

q: Propene + HBr (without peroxide) — what is the major product?
explanation: Markovnikov: Br goes to the more substituted carbon, via the more stable carbocation.
subject: Organic

q: Propene + HBr + peroxide — what is the major product?
explanation: The peroxide effect occurs only with HBr, by an anti-Markovnikov free-radical mechanism.
subject: Organic

q: What will be formed from But-2-yne + H2/Lindlar catalyst?
explanation: Syn-addition gives the cis-alkene; Na/liquid NH3 gives the trans-alkene.
subject: Organic

q: What is the major product of the nitration of nitrobenzene?
explanation: -NO2 is deactivating and meta-directing.
subject: Organic

q: Which alkyl bromide is the most reactive in SN2?
explanation: Less steric hindrance: methyl > 1° > 2° > 3°.
subject: Organic

q: What is the product of the SN1 reaction of optically pure (R)-2-bromobutane?
options: Partially racemised butan-2-ol (excess of the inverted enantiomer)
explanation: Attack occurs from both sides of the planar carbocation, so partial racemisation occurs — not a completely 50:50 racemic mixture, some excess of inversion also remains due to the ion pair; in SN2, backside attack causes Walden inversion.
subject: Organic

q: Phenol + CHCl3 + aq. NaOH (hot) — what is the major product?
explanation: Reimer-Tiemann, :CCl2 electrophile, ortho -CHO.
subject: Organic

q: Which compound will give the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH?
explanation: It should not have an alpha-H; benzaldehyde has no alpha-H.
subject: Organic

q: Acetaldehyde + dil. NaOH — what is the aldol product?
explanation: A beta-hydroxy aldehyde; on heating it gives crotonaldehyde.
subject: Organic

q: What is the basicity order of methyl amines in aqueous solution?
explanation: In aqueous solution there is a balance of the +I effect, solvation and steric effects; the gas-phase order is different (3° > 2° > 1°).
subject: Organic

q: What can be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
explanation: Only a pure 1° aliphatic amine; an aryl halide does not undergo SN2, so aniline is not formed.
subject: Organic

q: What will be formed from CH3MgBr + dry CO2, then H+/H2O?
explanation: The Grignard reagent adds to CO2, giving a carboxylic acid with one extra carbon; dry conditions are essential.
subject: Organic

q: Skraup synthesis: aniline + glycerol + conc. H2SO4 + nitrobenzene gives which heterocycle?
explanation: Glycerol gives acrolein; ring formation + oxidation gives quinoline.
subject: Organic

q: Which sugar is non-reducing?
explanation: In sucrose, both C-1 and C-2 are involved in the glycosidic bond, so there is no free aldehyde/keto group.
subject: Organic

q: What type of polymer is Nylon-6,6 and what are its monomers?
options: Condensation polyester; ethylene glycol + terephthalic acid
explanation: -CO-NH- amide linkage; Nylon-6 is obtained from caprolactam.
subject: Organic

q: [Numerical] At 300 K, what is the crms of O2 (M=0.032 kg/mol)? R=8.314.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] Van der Waals constants a = 1.39 L² atm mol⁻², b = 0.0391 L mol⁻¹; R = 0.0821 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. What is Tc?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] Bragg n=1, lambda=154 pm, theta=14.3°, sin≈0.247, what is d?
subject: Physical

q: What are the structures of NaCl and CsCl?
options: CsCl has a face-centred cubic (FCC) Bravais lattice
explanation: NaCl: Cl⁻ forms an FCC lattice with Na⁺ in the octahedral voids (6:6, Z = 4). CsCl is a primitive cubic lattice with a Cs⁺/Cl⁻ basis, loosely called a BCC arrangement of ions, not a BCC Bravais lattice (8:8, Z = 1).
subject: Physical

q: Schottky vs Frenkel?
options: In Schottky, equal numbers of cations/anions are missing and density decreases; in Frenkel, the small cation goes to an interstitial site and density is unchanged
explanation: In a Schottky defect, equal numbers of cations and anions are missing from the lattice, so density decreases; in a Frenkel defect, the small cation moves to an interstitial site and remains inside the lattice, so density remains unchanged.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] First-order t1/2=30 min, what is the time taken for 90% completion?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] Ea=50 kJ/mol, from 300K to 310K, what is k2/k1?
subject: Physical

q: Order vs molecularity?
options: Order is experimental and can be zero/fractional; molecularity is theoretical, only for an elementary step, and cannot be zero/fractional
Order is obtained from the coefficients of the balanced equation
explanation: Order is determined experimentally from the rate law, so it can be zero or fractional; molecularity is the number of particles taking part in an elementary step, so it is always a positive integer.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] 6.0 g solute, 100 g water, ΔTf=0.93 K, Kf=1.86, what is the molar mass?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] 0.05 M NaCl, 300 K, i=2, what is the osmotic pressure?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] 2 mol ideal gas, 300 K, isothermal reversible expansion from 10 L to 20 L, what is w?
subject: Physical

q: When is a reaction spontaneous at all T (ΔG always negative)?
options: ΔH positive, ΔS positive, low T
ΔH negative, ΔS negative, high T
explanation: When ΔH is negative and ΔS is positive, −TΔS is also always negative, so ΔG = ΔH − TΔS is negative at all temperatures.
subject: Physical

q: What is Hess's law?
options: On reversing an equation the sign of ΔH changes, and on multiplying the coefficients ΔH is multiplied
On reversing, ΔH remains the same
explanation: Enthalpy is a state function, so ΔH depends only on the initial and final states, not on the path (Hess's law: the ΔH of the overall reaction equals the sum of the ΔH values of its steps). Hence reversing an equation reverses the sign of ΔH, and multiplying the coefficients multiplies ΔH by the same factor.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] N2O4 ⇌ 2NO2, 298 K, Kc=0.20 mol/L, what is Kp?
subject: Physical

q: Le Chatelier?
options: A catalyst changes the equilibrium position
Inert gas at constant volume causes a shift
Increasing pressure shifts the equilibrium towards fewer gaseous moles
explanation: Only T changes K; a catalyst only reduces the time taken; inert gas at constant volume causes no shift.
subject: Physical

q: At the triple point of water, what is F? C=1, P=3.
explanation: F=C-P+2=0; invariant, T and P are fixed.
subject: Physical

q: Why is the slope of the ice-water fusion curve negative in the phase diagram of water?
options: The density of ice is greater than that of water
Volume decreases on melting, and increasing pressure lowers the melting point
explanation: Ice is less dense than water; pressure favours melting.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] Daniel cell E°=1.10 V, n=2, what is ΔG°? F=96500.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] 298 K, Zn|Zn2+ (0.01 M)||Cu2+ (0.1 M)|Cu, E°=1.10 V, what is the EMF?
subject: Physical

q: On dilution, what happens to specific conductance (κ) and molar conductance (Λm)?
explanation: On dilution there are fewer ions per unit volume, so κ decreases; Λm increases — for weak electrolytes because dissociation increases, and for strong electrolytes because interionic attraction decreases.
subject: Physical

q: How many radial nodes and angular nodes are there in a 3d orbital?
explanation: Radial nodes = n-l-1 = 3-2-1 = 0 and angular nodes = l = 2.
subject: Inorganic

q: According to the (n+l) rule, which orbital, 4s or 3d, fills first?
explanation: For 4s, (n+l) = 4 and for 3d it is 5, so 4s, with the lower (n+l), fills first.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which of the following sets of quantum numbers is impossible?
explanation: The value of l ranges from 0 to (n-1), so l=2 is impossible for n=2.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the correct order of ionic radii of the isoelectronic species N3-, O2-, F- and Na+?
explanation: All have 10 electrons, so the nucleus with more protons pulls the electron cloud more strongly towards itself and the radius is smaller.
subject: Inorganic

q: Whose electronegativity is the highest on the Pauling scale?
explanation: The electronegativity of fluorine is 4.0 on the Pauling scale, which is the highest.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is the second ionisation energy of sodium much higher than the first?
options: The second electron affinity of sodium is higher
The size of Na+ is larger than that of Na
The second electron is removed from a stable octet (neon configuration)
The second electron is removed from the 3s orbital
explanation: On removing the first electron, the stable octet of Na+ is formed; removing an electron from it is very difficult.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the shape of the SF4 molecule?
explanation: SF4 has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair; the lone pair occupies the equatorial position, so the shape is see-saw.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the bond order of the O2+ ion?
explanation: O2+ has 10 bonding electrons and 5 antibonding electrons, so bond order = (10-5)/2 = 2.5.
subject: Inorganic

q: In which of the following chlorides is the covalent character the greatest?
explanation: Al3+ is a small and highly charged cation, which polarises the electron cloud of Cl- the most (Fajans rule).
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is the boiling point of H2O much higher than that of H2S, although the molar mass of H2S is higher?
options: The molar mass of H2O is higher
There is strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in H2O, but not in H2S
Sulphur is more electronegative than oxygen
Hydrogen bonding is greater in H2S
explanation: Oxygen is small and more electronegative, so a strong hydrogen bond forms between H2O molecules.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is K2CO3 not made by the Solvay process?
options: Potassium is less reactive than sodium
NH3 does not react with KCl
CaCO3 does not react with K2CO3
KHCO3 is more soluble in water and does not precipitate
explanation: In the Solvay process NaHCO3 precipitates because it is less soluble, but KHCO3, being more soluble, does not precipitate.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is obtained by gentle heating of gypsum?
explanation: Gypsum, CaSO4·2H2O, on heating loses 3/2 water to form Plaster of Paris, CaSO4·1/2H2O.
subject: Inorganic

q: What type of acid is boric acid (H3BO3)?
explanation: H3BO3 does not directly give a proton, but accepts OH- to form [B(OH)4]-, so it is a weak monobasic Lewis acid.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which is the strongest acid among the oxo-acids of chlorine?
explanation: As the oxidation state increases, the negative charge of the conjugate base ClO4- is delocalised over 4 oxygens, so HClO4 is the strongest.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the shape of XeO3?
explanation: XeO3 has sp3 hybridisation, 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, so the shape is pyramidal.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is Zn not considered a transition element?
options: The d-subshell of Zn always remains full (d10); it has no incomplete d-orbital
Zn does not form any coloured compound, so it is not considered
The atomic number of Zn is low
Zn is not in the d-block
explanation: The definition of a transition element requires an incomplete d-orbital; in Zn, Cd and Hg, d10 always remains full.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the spin-only magnetic moment of the Ni2+ ion (d8, 2 unpaired electrons)?
subject: Inorganic

q: Why are the atomic/ionic radii of Zr and Hf almost equal?
options: Both have exactly the same electron configuration
Both are in the same group, so the radii are equal
explanation: Shielding by 4f electrons is very poor, so the radius decreases continuously from La to Lu and the radius of Hf becomes equal to that of Zr.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is the colour of KMnO4 purple, although the configuration of Mn(VII) is d0?
explanation: Mn(VII) has no d-electron, so the colour is not due to a d-d transition, but due to charge transfer from oxygen to manganese.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the Effective Atomic Number (EAN) of the [Co(NH3)6]3+ complex?
explanation: EAN = Z - oxidation number + 2 × coordination number = 27 - 3 + 12 = 36, which is equal to that of krypton.
subject: Inorganic

q: [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+ and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+ are examples of which type of isomerism?
explanation: NO2- is an ambidentate ligand, which forms nitro when bound through nitrogen and nitrito when bound through oxygen, so it is linkage isomerism.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which is the strongest-field ligand in the spectrochemical series?
explanation: In the spectrochemical series CO causes the greatest crystal field splitting, so it is the strongest-field ligand.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which statement about crystal field splitting (Δt) and spin in a tetrahedral complex is correct?
options: Δt = Δo and the complex is low-spin
Δt = (4/9)Δo and the complex is almost always high-spin
No splitting occurs in a tetrahedral complex
explanation: Tetrahedral splitting is much smaller than octahedral splitting, so Δt never exceeds the pairing energy and the complex remains high-spin.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why is BF3 a Lewis acid?
options: It accepts an electron pair, because the octet of boron is incomplete
explanation: Boron in BF3 has only 6 electrons, so it accepts an electron pair to complete its octet.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which of the following oxides is an amphoteric oxide?
explanation: Al2O3 reacts with both acid and base, so it is amphoteric; Na2O is basic, CO is neutral and SO3 is an acidic oxide.
subject: Inorganic

q: How does one chlorine radical destroy thousands of ozone molecules?
options: Chlorine combines with oxygen to form ozone
Chlorine reacts with ozone and is consumed
Chlorine is regenerated in the catalytic cycle and repeatedly breaks down ozone
Ozone breaks down by itself; chlorine has no role
explanation: In the cycle Cl + O3 → ClO + O2 and ClO + O → Cl + O2, chlorine is regenerated, so one Cl radical can destroy many O3 molecules.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which metal cluster is present in the nitrogenase enzyme for N2 fixation?
explanation: Nitrogenase contains an iron-molybdenum-sulphur cofactor, which uses ATP energy to break the triple bond of N2 to form ammonia.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which statement about heavy water (D2O) is correct?
options: There is no hydrogen bonding in D2O
D2O acts as a moderator in a nuclear reactor
The density of D2O is less than that of H2O
explanation: The density of D2O is 1.11 g/mL and it slows neutrons without absorbing them much, so it is used as a moderator.
subject: Inorganic

q: According to the Ellingham diagram, why is Al2O3 not reduced by carbon?
options: The line of carbon is below the line of aluminium
The melting point of Al2O3 is very low
Carbon is less reactive than aluminium
The line of aluminium is below the line of carbon/CO, so Al2O3 is more stable
explanation: The ΔG of formation of aluminium oxide is more negative than that of carbon oxide, so carbon cannot reduce Al2O3; aluminium is extracted by the electrolytic method.
subject: Inorganic

q: Why does the white precipitate formed with AgNO3 in the identification of Cl- dissolve in NH4OH?
options: AgCl forms the [Ag(NH3)2]+ complex with NH4OH, so it dissolves
The white precipitate is not AgCl
explanation: AgCl forms the soluble diammine silver(I) complex [Ag(NH3)2]+ with ammonia, so it dissolves; the Ksp of AgI is very low, so it does not dissolve in NH4OH.
subject: Inorganic

q: In which compound is the carbon-carbon bond the shortest?
explanation: As bond order increases, bond length decreases; the triple bond is the shortest and strongest.
subject: Organic

q: Which of the following compounds is anti-aromatic?
explanation: Cyclobutadiene is planar, cyclic and conjugated and has 4π electrons, so according to the Hückel rule it is anti-aromatic.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the most stable carbanion?
explanation: The stability of a carbanion is the opposite of that of a carbocation: CH3− > 1° > 2° > 3°, because the +I effect of the alkyl group increases the negative charge.
subject: Organic

q: Which of the following is NOT an electrophile?
explanation: NH3 has a lone pair of electrons, so it is a nucleophile; all the others are electron-pair acceptor electrophiles.
subject: Organic

q: What is the maximum number of stereoisomers possible for a compound with 3 stereogenic centres and no symmetry?
explanation: Maximum stereoisomers = 2^n; when n = 3, 2³ = 8.
subject: Organic

q: Which of the following compounds shows geometrical isomerism?
explanation: In But-2-ene both carbons of C=C have different groups, so cis/trans forms are possible; in the others, one carbon has two identical H atoms.
subject: Organic

q: How many alkane products in total are formed by the Wurtz reaction of a mixture of CH3Br and C2H5Br?
explanation: Ethane, propane and butane — three products are formed, so the Wurtz reaction is not suitable for unsymmetrical alkanes.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the most stable conformation of cyclohexane?
explanation: In the chair form, torsional strain and 1,3-diaxial repulsion are minimum, so it is the most stable.
subject: Organic

q: What is the main product of the hydroboration-oxidation of propene (B2H6/THF, then H2O2/NaOH)?
explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation is anti-Markovnikov addition; –OH attaches to the less substituted carbon, so propan-1-ol is formed.
subject: Organic

q: What is obtained by the reductive ozonolysis (O3, then Zn/H2O) of But-2-ene?
options: 1 molecule of acetaldehyde + 1 molecule of formaldehyde
explanation: The C=C bond breaks and both carbons form acetaldehyde (CH3CHO), so 2 molecules of acetaldehyde are obtained.
subject: Organic

q: Which compound gives a white precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO3?
explanation: Only a terminal alkyne (R–C≡C–H) has an acidic H, which is replaced by Ag+ to give a white silver acetylide precipitate.
subject: Organic

q: What are the main products of the nitration of toluene?
explanation: –CH3 is an activating and o/p-directing group, so the electrophile goes mainly to the ortho and para positions.
subject: Organic

q: What is the main product of the Birch reduction of benzene (Na/liquid NH3 + EtOH)?
explanation: In Birch reduction, partial reduction of benzene gives the unconjugated 1,4-cyclohexadiene.
subject: Organic

q: Why is chlorobenzene much less reactive than chloroethane in nucleophilic substitution?
options: The –I effect of Cl is very low
Due to resonance, the C–Cl bond acquires partial double-bond character
The size of the Cl atom is very large
explanation: The lone pair of Cl is delocalised in the ring, making the C–Cl bond shorter and stronger and difficult to break.
subject: Organic
topic: Alkyl and Aryl Halides — Haloarene Inertness

q: Which aryl halide is the most reactive towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution?
explanation: Two –NO2 groups at o/p positions stabilise the Meisenheimer complex by resonance, so the reaction is the fastest.
subject: Organic
topic: Alkyl and Aryl Halides — Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution

q: Which alcohol gives immediate turbidity in the Lucas test (conc. HCl + ZnCl2)?
explanation: A 3° alcohol immediately forms the chloride because the 3° carbocation is the most stable; a 1° alcohol does not give turbidity at room temperature.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the most acidic phenol derivative?
explanation: The –NO2 electron-withdrawing group stabilises the phenoxide ion, so p-nitrophenol is the most acidic.
subject: Organic

q: What is formed on heating diethyl ether with excess HI?
explanation: Excess HI breaks both C–O bonds and both alkyl groups change into iodides.
subject: Organic

q: Which compound does NOT give a silver mirror with Tollens reagent?
explanation: Ketones do not reduce Tollens reagent; aldehydes and formic acid give a silver mirror.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the strongest acid?
explanation: As the number of Cl atoms increases, the –I effect increases and the carboxylate ion becomes more stable, so trichloroacetic acid is the strongest.
subject: Organic

q: Which amine gives a foul-smelling isocyanide in the carbylamine test?
explanation: Only a 1° amine, on heating with CHCl3 and alcoholic KOH, forms an isocyanide; 2° and 3° amines do not give this test.
subject: Organic

q: At what temperature is the diazotisation of aniline carried out?
explanation: The diazonium salt decomposes above 5°C, so diazotisation is carried out in an ice-cold solution (0–5°C).
subject: Organic

q: What is the main product of the Br2/NaOH (Hofmann bromamide) reaction of CH3CONH2?
explanation: In the Hofmann bromamide reaction, an amide changes into an amine with one carbon fewer, so CH3NH2 is formed.
subject: Organic

q: What is formed after the reaction of CH3MgBr with formaldehyde (HCHO) followed by hydrolysis (work-up)?
explanation: The Grignard reagent adds to formaldehyde to give a 1° alcohol with one extra carbon, so ethanol is formed.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the correct order of basicity?
explanation: The lone pair of piperidine is sp3 and available; the lone pair of pyridine is available but sp2; the lone pair of pyrrole is part of the aromatic sextet.
subject: Organic

q: Which heterocyclic compound is formed by the Paal-Knorr reaction of hexane-2,5-dione with NH3?
explanation: A 1,4-diketone condenses with NH3 to form the pyrrole ring; P2O5 gives furan and P2S5 gives thiophene.
subject: Organic

q: Why do glucose, fructose and mannose give the same osazone with phenylhydrazine?
options: Only C-1 and C-2 take part in osazone formation
All three have a different molecular formula
All three have the same number of –OH groups
explanation: Osazone formation occurs at C-1 and C-2, so the difference in configuration at these carbons disappears and the osazone of all three is the same.
subject: Organic

q: What does the iodine value measure?
options: Unsaturation (number of double bonds) in fat
explanation: The iodine value is the amount of I2 absorbed by 100 g of fat; a higher iodine value means more double bonds, i.e. more unsaturation.
subject: Organic
topic: Fat, Oils and Detergents — Iodine Value

q: Which of the following is a thermosetting polymer, which cannot be remoulded on heating?
explanation: Bakelite is a cross-linked thermosetting polymer of phenol and formaldehyde; on heating it becomes hard and does not remould.
subject: Organic

q: Which group in a dye is the chromophore that gives colour?
explanation: –N=N– (azo) is the chromophore group that gives colour, while –OH and –NH2 are auxochromes that deepen the colour.
subject: Organic

q: [Numerical] At the same temperature and pressure, how many times will the diffusion rate of H₂ be compared to that of O₂? (M_H₂ = 2, M_O₂ = 32)
explanation: By Graham's law, r ∝ 1/√M, so r_H₂/r_O₂ = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] The total pressure of a gas mixture is 760 mmHg and the mole fraction of one gas in it is 0.25. What will be the partial pressure of that gas?
explanation: By Dalton's law, p = x × P_total = 0.25 × 760 = 190 mmHg.
subject: Physical

q: What is the correct order of most probable velocity (cmp), average velocity (cav) and rms velocity (crms) for a gas?
explanation: Always cmp : cav : crms = 1 : 1.128 : 1.225, so cmp is the lowest and crms is the highest.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For CO₂, the van der Waals constants are a = 3.59 L² atm mol⁻² and b = 0.0427 L mol⁻¹. What will be its critical pressure (Pc) approximately?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] A metal crystallises in an FCC structure. a = 408 pm, M = 108 g/mol, Z = 4. What will be its density approximately? (Na = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical
topic: Solid State — Density of Unit Cell

q: If the cation/anion radius ratio is 0.50, what will be the coordination number and geometry?
explanation: The ratio 0.414–0.732 is for octahedral voids, so CN = 6 and an NaCl-type structure is formed.
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about the zinc blende (ZnS) structure is correct?
options: S²⁻ are in FCC and Zn²⁺ are in alternate tetrahedral voids; coordination is 4:4
Zn²⁺ are in FCC and S²⁻ are in all octahedral voids; coordination is 6:6
In ZnS there is only 1 formula unit per unit cell
explanation: In ZnS, S²⁻ form a CCP/FCC arrangement, Zn²⁺ occupy half the tetrahedral voids, Z = 4 and CN is 4:4.
subject: Physical

q: What colour does NaCl become due to an F-centre?
explanation: An electron trapped in an anion vacancy forms an F-centre, which gives NaCl a yellow colour.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a zero order reaction, [A]₀ = 0.20 mol L⁻¹ and k = 0.01 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. What will be its half-life (t₁/₂)?
explanation: For zero order, t₁/₂ = [A]₀/(2k) = 0.20/(2 × 0.01) = 10 s.
subject: Physical

q: In a second order reaction, what effect will doubling the initial concentration [A]₀ have on the half-life (t₁/₂)?
explanation: For second order, t₁/₂ = 1/(k[A]₀), so doubling [A]₀ halves t₁/₂.
subject: Physical

q: Which of the following is an example of a pseudo-first order reaction?
options: A bimolecular reaction between two gases
A saturated zero order reaction on a surface
explanation: Water being in excess, its concentration remains almost constant, so the actual second order reaction appears to be first order.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a first order reaction, t₁/₂ = 10 s. What will be its mean life approximately?
explanation: k = 0.693/10 = 0.0693 s⁻¹; mean life = 1/k ≈ 14.4 s, which is 1.44 × t₁/₂.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] In a solution, the mole fraction of the solute is 0.02 and the vapour pressure of the pure solvent is 100 mmHg. What will be the vapour pressure of the solution?
explanation: Relative lowering = x₂ = 0.02, so the decrease in pressure = 2 mmHg and the pressure of the solution = 100 − 2 = 98 mmHg.
subject: Physical
topic: Colligative Properties — Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure

q: [Numerical] What will be the boiling point elevation (ΔTb) for a 0.50 molal non-volatile solute solution? (Kb = 0.52 K kg mol⁻¹, i = 1)
subject: Physical
topic: Colligative Properties — Elevation of Boiling Point

q: [Numerical] The degree of dissociation (α) of CaCl₂ is 0.90. What will be its van't Hoff factor (i)?
explanation: For n = 3 particles, i = 1 + (n − 1)α = 1 + 2 × 0.90 = 2.8.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] What is the freezing point depression (ΔTf) for a 0.10 molal aqueous solution of a non-volatile non-electrolyte? (Kf = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a reaction at 298 K, ΔU = −100 kJ/mol and Δng = −2. What will ΔH be approximately? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] In the adiabatic reversible expansion of 1 mol of a diatomic ideal gas (γ = 1.4) at 300 K, the volume becomes 8 times. What will be the final temperature approximately?
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about the heat of neutralisation is correct?
options: It is more negative for a weak acid
It is the same for all acid-base pairs
The heat of neutralisation is always positive
For a strong acid + strong base it is approximately −57.1 kJ/mol; for a weak acid/base it is less negative because some heat is spent in ionisation
explanation: The actual reaction is H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O; in a weak acid/base, heat spent in ionisation makes the value less negative.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] At 298 K, the equilibrium constant K = 10 for a reaction. What will ΔG° be approximately?
subject: Physical
topic: Thermodynamics — Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

q: For which reaction will Kp = Kc?
explanation: In H2 + I2 ⇌ 2HI, Δng = 2 − 2 = 0, so Kp = Kc(RT)^0 = Kc. In the other reactions Δng ≠ 0.
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Kp and Kc Relation

q: [Numerical] For the reaction A ⇌ B, Kc = 4. Initially [A] = 1.0 M and [B] = 0. What will [B] be at equilibrium?
explanation: From Kc = x/(1 − x) = 4, x = 0.80, so at equilibrium [B] = 0.80 M.
subject: Physical

q: For an exothermic reaction, what effect will increasing the temperature have on the equilibrium constant (K)?
options: K will first increase then decrease
explanation: According to Le Chatelier, increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic direction, so the K of an exothermic reaction decreases.
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Temperature Effect on K

q: [Numerical] The molar solubility (s) of a salt of type AB₂ is 1 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹. What will be its solubility product (Ksp)?
explanation: For AB₂, Ksp = 4s³ = 4 × (10⁻³)³ = 4 × 10⁻⁹.
subject: Physical

q: In a two-component system, 2 phases are in equilibrium and the pressure is constant. By the reduced phase rule, what will be the degree of freedom (F')?
explanation: F' = C − P + 1 = 2 − 2 + 1 = 1, so the system is univariant.
subject: Physical

q: In a one-component system, what is the maximum number of phases that can coexist in equilibrium?
explanation: Setting F = C − P + 2 = 0 gives P = 3; more phases would make F negative, which is not possible.
subject: Physical

q: On the sublimation curve (OB) in the phase diagram of water, which phases remain in equilibrium and what is the degree of freedom?
explanation: On OB there is ice ⇌ vapour equilibrium; with P = 2, F = 1 − 2 + 2 = 1 (univariant).
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] The specific conductance (κ) of a 0.10 M solution is 0.020 S cm⁻¹. What is its molar conductance (Λm)?
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] On passing 1 Faraday (1 F) of charge, how much copper (Cu) will be deposited from a Cu²⁺ solution? (Atomic weight of Cu = 63.5)
explanation: The equivalent weight of Cu = 63.5/2 = 31.75 g, and 1 F liberates 1 gram-equivalent of a substance.
subject: Physical

q: Which statement about standard electrode potential (E°) is correct?
options: On multiplying the coefficients of the equation, E° does not change, because it is an intensive property
On doubling the equation, E° also doubles
E° does not depend on temperature
explanation: Potential is an intensive property; ΔG changes, E° does not. E° can also be negative and can change with temperature.
subject: Physical

q: Which of the following is the correct order of first ionisation enthalpy (increasing order)?
explanation: First ionisation enthalpies (kJ mol⁻¹) are approximately Al 578 < Mg 738 < Si 787 < P 1012. Al is lower than Mg because its outer electron is in a 3p orbital rather than the stable filled 3s² subshell, and P is highest because of its stable half-filled 3p³ configuration.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the shape of ClF₃?
explanation: ClF₃ has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs; the lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, so the shape is T-shaped.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the bond order of the O₂⁻ ion?
explanation: The bond order of O₂ is 2; one extra electron goes into a π* antibonding orbital, so bond order = (10 − 7)/2 = 1.5.
subject: Inorganic

q: The aqueous solution of which ion is colourless?
explanation: The configuration of Zn²⁺ is d¹⁰; a d–d transition is not possible, so the solution is colourless.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is the Effective Atomic Number (EAN) of [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻?
explanation: EAN = atomic number − oxidation state + 2 × number of ligands = 26 − 2 + 12 = 36, which is equal to Kr.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which species is amphiprotic, i.e. can behave as both an acid and a base?
explanation: HCO₃⁻ can give H⁺ to form CO₃²⁻ and take H⁺ to form H₂CO₃; CO₃²⁻ is only a base and NH₄⁺ is only an acid.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which metal ion is at the centre of chlorophyll?
explanation: At the centre of the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll is Mg²⁺; Fe²⁺ is in haemoglobin.
subject: Inorganic

q: Which is the most stable free radical?
explanation: In the benzyl radical, the unpaired electron is delocalised by resonance in the benzene ring, so it is more stable than even a tertiary radical.
subject: Organic

q: How many stereoisomers in total are there of CH₃–CHBr–CHBr–CH₃ (2,3-Dibromobutane)?
explanation: It has one meso form and one enantiomeric pair, a total of 3 stereoisomers.
subject: Organic

q: Which is the lowest-energy (most stable) conformation of n-butane?
explanation: In the anti staggered conformation, both methyl groups are farthest apart, so torsional and steric strain are minimum.
subject: Organic

q: Which alkene gives only acetone on ozonolysis?
explanation: Both sides of (CH₃)₂C=C(CH₃)₂ have (CH₃)₂C= groups, so ozonolysis gives only 2 molecules of acetone.
subject: Organic

q: Who is the most reactive towards electrophilic aromatic substitution?
explanation: The –CH₃ group activates the ring by the +I effect and hyperconjugation; –NO₂ and –Cl deactivate the ring.
subject: Organic

q: In the reaction of 2-bromobutane with alc. KOH, which is the major product?
explanation: By the Saytzeff rule, the more substituted alkene is formed; trans-But-2-ene, being more stable than cis, is the major product.
subject: Organic

q: Which of the following compounds does NOT give the iodoform test?
explanation: The iodoform test requires a CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– group; formaldehyde has no methyl group, so it does not give the test.
subject: Organic

q: Who forms a diazonium salt with NaNO₂ + HCl at 0–5 °C?
explanation: Only a primary aromatic amine (aniline) forms a stable diazonium salt; an aliphatic primary amine is destroyed giving N₂ gas.
subject: Organic

q: How many hydrogen bonds are there between Guanine (G) and Cytosine (C) in DNA?
explanation: The G–C pair has 3 hydrogen bonds, while the A–T pair has 2 hydrogen bonds.
subject: Organic

q: [Numerical] At 300 K, what will be the average translational kinetic energy of 1 mol of an ideal gas? (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
explanation: Average translational KE = (3/2)RT = 1.5 × 8.314 × 300 = 3741 J ≈ 3.74 kJ.
subject: Physical

q: [Numerical] For a reaction, rate = k[A]². On increasing [A] 3 times, how many times will the rate increase?
explanation: Rate is proportional to the square of [A], so the rate will increase 3² = 9 times.
subject: Physical

q: Which colligative property is most suitable for determining the molar mass of proteins and other macromolecules, and why?
options: Osmotic pressure, because it gives a large, accurately measurable value even at the very low concentrations at which macromolecules dissolve
Elevation of boiling point, because proteins are stable on heating
Depression of freezing point, because it gives the largest change
Relative lowering of vapour pressure, because it is independent of temperature
explanation: Osmotic pressure is used for macromolecules because, unlike the elevation of boiling point or the depression of freezing point, it is large enough to measure accurately at very low concentrations, and it is measured at room temperature, so the solute is not heated or damaged.
subject: Physical

q: How many effective atoms are there in an FCC (face-centred cubic) unit cell?
explanation: 8 corners × 1/8 + 6 faces × 1/2 = 1 + 3 = 4 atoms per unit cell.
subject: Physical

q: In which process is the increase in entropy the greatest?
explanation: On changing directly from a solid to a gas, disorder increases the most; in the other three processes entropy decreases.
subject: Physical

q: In the exothermic Haber process N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, which condition is best to increase the yield of NH₃?
explanation: In an exothermic reaction, low temperature favours the forward direction and high pressure favours the direction with fewer gaseous moles (to the right).
subject: Physical
topic: Chemical Equilibrium — Haber Process, Le Chatelier

q: Which of the following is an example of homogeneous catalysis?
options: Fe catalyst in the Haber process
explanation: In ester hydrolysis, H₂SO₄ is in the same phase (liquid) as the reactants; in the other three, the catalyst is solid and the reactants are gas/liquid.
subject: Physical

q: What is the phenomenon of scattering of light by colloidal particles called?
explanation: The path of a light ray passing through a colloidal solution is visible due to the Tyndall effect.
subject: Physical

q: According to Fajans rules, which compound will have the most covalent character?
explanation: Li+ is the smallest cation, its polarising power is the greatest, so LiCl has the most covalent character.
subject: Inorganic

q: What is formed on reducing KMnO4 in a strong alkaline medium?
explanation: In a strong alkaline medium, MnO4- takes one electron to form green MnO4 2-, in which the oxidation state of Mn is +6.
subject: Inorganic

q: When is rain called acid rain?
options: When its pH is equal to 7.0
When its pH is less than 6.8
When its pH is less than 5.6
When its pH is less than 7.0
explanation: Due to CO2, the pH of normal rain is about 5.6; when the pH falls below 5.6 due to SO2 and NOx, it is called acid rain.
subject: Inorganic

q: The Mond process is used for the refining of which metal?
explanation: In the Mond process, Ni + 4CO forms volatile Ni(CO)4, which on heating gives pure Ni.
subject: Inorganic

q: According to the Huckel rule, which species is aromatic?
explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion has 6 pi-electrons and is cyclic, planar and conjugated, so by the (4n+2) rule it is aromatic.
subject: Organic

q: In the chlorobenzene + NaNH2 / liq. NH3 reaction, what is formed via the benzyne intermediate?
explanation: Attack of NH2- on the benzyne intermediate forms aniline; this is the elimination-addition mechanism.
subject: Organic

q: At which position does electrophilic substitution occur preferentially in pyrrole?
explanation: Electrophilic substitution in pyrrole occurs preferentially at the 2-position (α-position), because the intermediate formed by attack at C-2 is stabilised by resonance to a greater extent than the intermediate formed by attack at C-3.
subject: Organic

q: Which aldehyde does NOT reduce Fehling solution?
explanation: The aromatic aldehyde benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling solution, but gives a silver mirror with Tollens reagent.
subject: Organic

q: Acetic acid dimerises completely in benzene. What is its van't Hoff factor (i)?
explanation: Two acetic acid molecules associate to form one dimer particle, so the number of particles is halved and i = 1/2 = 0.5. The observed molar mass is therefore twice the normal molar mass.
subject: Physical

q: What does a compressibility factor Z < 1 mean?
explanation: Z = PV/RT; Z < 1 means the gas shows less volume than ideal due to intermolecular attraction.
subject: Physical

q: What is the packing efficiency of an FCC (face-centred cubic) crystal?
explanation: The packing efficiency in FCC is 74%, in BCC 68% and in simple cubic 52.4%.
subject: Physical

q: Multilayer adsorption is possible in which type of adsorption?
explanation: Physisorption occurs by weak van der Waals forces and can form multilayers; in chemisorption, due to the chemical bond only a monolayer is formed.
subject: Physical

q: For 1 mol of an ideal gas, what is the value of CP - CV?
explanation: For an ideal gas, CP - CV = R, where R is the gas constant.
subject: Physical

q: According to Henry law, what is the effect on the solubility of a gas?
options: The solubility of a gas increases on increasing pressure
The solubility of a gas is always independent of temperature
The solubility of a gas decreases on increasing pressure
The solubility of a gas is independent of pressure
explanation: According to Henry law, the solubility of a gas is proportional to its partial pressure, so solubility increases on increasing pressure.
subject: Physical
